question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution: The correct answer is **"to."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • **"To" **is the correct preposition to use in this context, as it indicates movement from one side of something to the other. • **"To" **means in the direction of; as far as. (की दिशा में, की ओर; जहाँ तक) • **Example**: *She’s going **to**__ Chennai.* • The other options do not make sense grammatically in this context. • The correct answer is Option 2. • Correct passage: My breath is halted, like gasping for air __after__ crying far too long and hard. It is like a hiccup, with a shivering sharpness __of__ nerves. It is like icicles running __down__ your spine or aluminum in your mouth, an eerie amount of emotions that cannot compare **__to__ **the actual feelings you’ve managed to live ______ (5) ______. I just watched you die; I say to myself silently.​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** • **Option 1, "away"**, indicates movement in the opposite direction of "across". (भिन्‍न स्‍थान या दिशा में; दूर) • **Option 3, "inside"**, indicates being within something rather than crossing over it. (किसी वस्‍तु के अंदरूनी भाग या सतह में/पर/की ओर, के भीतर, के अंदर, अंदर या भीतर के) • **Option 4, "across**", indicating from one side of something to the other. (एक ओर से दूसरी ओर; आर-पार) 41:Tda7, The correct answer is **"through."**
